U.S. Department of Energy ORDER 
 Washington, D.C.  
 
Approved: 08-05-2026 
 
SUBJECT:  MANAGEMENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY NUCLEAR 
SECURITY ENTERPRISE 
1. OBJECTIVES. 
a. To establish the authorities and responsibilities of the National Nuclear Security 
Administration (NNSA) for management of the Department of Energy (DOE) 
Nuclear Security Enterprise (NSE). 
b. To establish operational guidelines and administrative procedures for NNSA and 
contractor management of NSE capabilities and resources used to manage the 
nuclear weapons mission, DOE’s non-weapon responsibilities, and other 
programs of national interest. 
2. CANCELLATION.  DOE Order (O) 452.3, Management of the Department of Energy 
Nuclear Weapons Complex, dated June 8, 2005.  Cancellation of an Order does not, by 
itself, modify or otherwise affect any contractual obligation to comply with the Order.  
Canceled Orders that are incorporated by reference in a contract remain in effect until the 
contract is modified to delete the references to the requirements in the canceled Orders. 
3. APPLICABILITY. 
a. DOE Elements.  Except for the exclusion in paragraph 3c, this Order applies to 
NNSA employees and other DOE elements that are involved in or interact with 
management of the NSE. 
b. NSE Contractors. 
(1) Except for the exclusions in paragraph 3c, the Contractor Requirements 
Document (CRD), Attachment 1, sets forth requirements of this Order that 
will apply to contractors whose contracts of which involve the 
management, design, construction, operations, and decommissioning of 
defense nuclear facilities; or equipment or any activities involving the 
storage, handling, or use of special nuclear materials, radioactive 
materials, high explosives, and high-intensity lasers. 
(2) An affected contractor is responsible for flowing down requirements of 
this CRD to subcontractors at any tier to the extent necessary to ensure 
contractor compliance with the requirements. 
DOE O 452.3A

c. Exclusions. 
(1) Activities conducted under the authority of the Director, Naval Nuclear 
Propulsion Program, pursuant to Executive Order 12344, as set forth in 
Public Law (P.L.) 98-525, Department of Energy National Security and 
Military Applications of Nuclear Energy Authorization Act of 1985, and 
P.L. 106-65, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2000. 
(2) All DOE elements are excluded from this Order except for the Office of 
the Secretary; and the NNSA. 
4. REQUIREMENTS. 
a. The Unites States (U.S.) nuclear weapons mission will be the highest priority in 
the planning, programming, budgeting, execution, and evaluation of NSE work. 
b. In accordance with P.L. 107-296, Homeland Security Act of 2002, and consistent 
with resources provided, Department of Homeland Security (DHS) projects will 
be prioritized on an equal basis with the nuclear weapons program and given 
higher priority status than strategic partnership projects (SPPs). 
Notwithstanding any other law governing the administration, 
mission, use, or operations of any of the Department of Energy 
national laboratories and sites, such laboratories and sites are 
authorized to accept and perform work for the Secretary, 
consistent with resources provided, and perform such work on an 
equal basis to other missions at the laboratory and not on a 
noninterference basis with other missions of such laboratory or 
site.  [6 United States Code (U.S.C.) 189(a)(2)] 
Situations in which conflicts arise between national security programs and the 
nuclear weapons program over competing priorities for limited technical 
resources will be brought to the attention of the NNSA Administrator through the 
Deputy Administrator for Defense Programs for coordination and resolution.  The 
Office of the Secretary of Energy is briefed on the resolution. 
c. Requests for NSE capabilities and resources in support of non-weapon missions 
or other programs of national interest will be accepted and conducted in such a 
manner as to avoid adverse impact or impediments to the management of the U.S. 
nuclear weapons mission. 
d. NSE nuclear weapons mission requirements will be prioritized, taking into 
account the following objectives: 
(1) Maintain and enhance the existing nuclear weapons mission in accordance 
with Presidential Directives and the President’s annual Nuclear Weapons 
Stockpile Memorandum in accordance with:

(a) DOE O 452.1B, Nuclear Explosive and Weapons Surety Program; 
(b) DOE O 452.2B, Safety of Nuclear Explosive Operations; 
(c) DOE O 452.4A, Security and Control of Nuclear Explosives and 
Nuclear Weapons; and 
(d) DOE O 414.1B, Quality Assurance. 
(2) Enhance NSE research and development and infrastructure to support 
applied research, development, testing, and production capabilities 
necessary to maintain the nuclear weapons mission, to support the annual 
stockpile assessment, to address scientific and engineering issues pertinent 
to stockpile stewardship, and to develop options for the future nuclear 
deterrent working with the Department of War. 
(3) Meet the immediate needs of the nuclear weapons mission as directed by 
the production and planning directive: 
(a) Replacing limited-life components; 
(b) Repairing weapons; and 
(c) Providing safe, secure transport of warheads, components, and 
nuclear materials. 
(4) Conduct surveillance of the stockpile to assess the safety, security, and 
reliability of the warheads, including disassembly and inspection of 
weapons, conducting flight and laboratory tests, developing enhanced 
surveillance techniques, and supporting the annual stockpile assessment. 
(5) Develop and maintain the responsive infrastructure necessary to support 
nuclear weapons mission needs. 
(6) Develop and apply comprehensive assessment methodologies, plans, and 
experimental tools to advance the understanding of scientific and technical 
issues affecting the safety, reliability, or performance of nuclear weapons. 
(7) Store and dismantle nuclear weapons removed from the stockpile safely 
and securely. 
(8) Manage the monitored storage and disposition of legacy and newly 
generated waste within the NSE in compliance with applicable Federal 
laws and regulations pertaining to protecting the environment, safety, 
and health.

(9) Use the established SPP administrative processes to confirm that projects 
requested by other Federal agencies through SPP channels will not 
interfere with nuclear weapons programs or create detrimental burdens on 
NNSA resources in the future. 
5. RESPONSIBILITIES. 
a. Secretary of Energy. 
(1) Establish DOE policy and objectives in accordance with national law, 
Presidential Directives, and other national-level policy, as required to 
inform management of NSE capabilities and resources for management of 
the nuclear weapons stockpile, the non-weapons mission, and other 
national security needs. 
b. NNSA Administrator. 
(1) Establish expectations and objectives for the prioritization and 
management of NSE capabilities and resources in accordance with 
50 U.S.C. Chapter 41 § 2401, Establishment and mission, et seq. 
Presidential Directives, Secretarial Directives, and other national-level 
policy, which inform management of NSE capabilities and resources for 
management of the nuclear weapons mission, the non-weapons mission, 
and other national security needs. 
(2) Ensure that work performed for DHS at NNSA is performed on an equal 
basis with and not on a noninterference basis with other missions of such 
laboratory missions (in accordance with the Homeland Security Act, 
Section 309[a][2]; 6 U.S.C. §189[a][2]). 
(3) Ensure that priority consideration is given non-weapon work related to 
compelling national security concerns and sponsored by the Department of 
War, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission, or U.S. Intelligence 
Community. 
(4) Ensures administration of the NSE contracts that are for the management 
and operations of national security laboratories, nuclear weapons 
production facilities, and sites and that include the CRD for this Order. 
c. NNSA Deputy Administrator for Defense Programs. 
(1) Establish expectations and objectives for managing the capabilities needed 
to design, produce, test, and maintain weapons to meet national 
security requirements. 
(2) Report directly to the NNSA Administrator in a timely manner all matters 
pertaining to availability of NSE resources, constraints, capabilities, 
performance, mission, and actual or potential conflicts in priorities to meet 
national security requirements.

(4) P.L. 108-136, National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal 
Year 2004; and 
(5) P.L. 108-375, Ronald W. Reagan National Defense Authorization Act for 
Fiscal Year 2005. 
b. P.L. 72-212, Economy Act of 1932, as amended (31 U.S.C. § 1535), which 
authorizes an agency to place orders for goods and services with another 
government agency when in the best interest of the government. 
c. P.L. 83-703, Atomic Energy Act of 1954, as amended (42 U.S.C. § 2011 et seq.), 
Sections 31, 32, and 33, which authorizes the conduct of research and 
development and certain training activities for non-DOE entities. 
d. P.L. 93-438, Energy Reorganization Act of 1974, Section 205 (42 U.S.C. § 5845), 
which requires Federal agencies to furnish to the Nuclear Regulatory 
Commission, on a reimbursable basis, such research services deemed necessary. 
e. P.L. 107-296, Homeland Security Act of 2002, Section 309(6 U.S.C. § 189(a)(2) 
requirements relating to utilization of Department of Energy national laboratories 
and sites in support of Homeland Security activities. 
f. Memorandum of Agreement (EXEC-2003-002486) between Department of 
Energy and Department of Homeland Security (February 28, 2003), which allows 
work directly funded by DHS to be accepted, performed, and administered in 
accordance with the terms of the memorandum of agreement. 
g. Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Subpart 17.5, “Interagency Acquisitions 
under the Economy Act.” 
h. FAR 35.017, “Federally Funded Research and Development Centers (FFRDCs).” 
i. NNSA Business Operating Plan (BOP) 006.001, “NNSA Program Management 
Policy,” dated August 12, 2004. 
j. DOE/NNSA Quality Criteria (QC) 1, “Weapon Quality Policy,” Rev. 10, 
February 10, 2004. 
k. DOE P 413.1, Program and Project Management Policy for the Planning, 
Programming, Budgeting, and Acquisition of Capital Assets, dated June 10, 2000, 
and Office of Management and Budget Circulars A-11, A-123, A-127, and A-130. 
l. DOE O 414.1B, Quality Assurance; DOE O 452.1B, Nuclear Explosive and 
Weapons Surety Program; DOE O 452.2B, Safety of Nuclear Explosive 
Operations; DOE O 452.4A, Security and Control of Nuclear Explosives and 
Nuclear Weapons; DOE O 470.1, Safeguards and Security Program; 
DOE N 481.1A, Reimbursable Work for Department of Homeland Security; 
DOE O 481.1C, Work-for-Others (Non-Department of Energy Funded Work); 
10 CFR 830.121, “Quality Assurance Requirements.”

8. CONTACT.  Questions concerning this Order should be addressed to the Office of the 
Deputy Administrator for Defense Programs. 
BY ORDER OF THE SECRETARY OF ENERGY: 
 
JAMES P. DANLY 
Deputy Secretary

ATTACHMENT 1 
CONTRACTOR REQUIREMENTS DOCUMENT 
DOE O 452.3, MANAGEMENT OF THE DEPARTMENT OF ENERGY NUCLEAR 
SECURITY ENTERPRISE 
This Contractor Requirements Document (CRD) establishes requirements for Department of 
Energy (DOE) and National Nuclear Security Administration (NNSA) Contractors within the 
DOE Nuclear Security Enterprise (NSE).  Regardless of the performer of the work, the 
contractor is responsible for complying with the requirements of this CRD and for flowing down 
requirements to subcontractors at any tier to the extent necessary to ensure compliance.  The 
contractor must not flow down requirements to subcontractors unnecessarily or imprudently and 
must incur only those costs that would be incurred by a prudent person in the conduct of 
competitive business. 
1. Manage facilities and sites of NSE in accordance with DOE policies, priorities, and 
objectives set forth in the requirements section of DOE O 452.3. 
2. Maintain the capabilities to design, produce, and test weapons to meet national security 
requirements in accordance with guidance and direction of the NNSA Deputy 
Administrator for Defense Programs. 
3. Document plans and program functions and identify fiscal requirements for NSE 
missions to support DOE budget planning. 
4. Submit to the NNSA site office long-range projections of work to be accomplished 
including strategic partnership projects (SPPs) to support DOE and NNSA institutional 
planning requirements. 
5. Notify NNSA when there is actual or potential for adverse impact of SPP work on the 
ability to support the nuclear weapons program. 
6. Support DOE’s non-weapon responsibilities or other programs of national interest as 
directed while ensuring that this work does not impact or impede management of the U.S. 
nuclear weapons mission. 
7. Manage NSE facilities and programs in a manner consistent with the following national 
security mission requirements: 
a. Conduct stockpile surveillance to assess the safety, security, and reliability of the 
weapons including disassembly and inspection of weapons, conducting flight and 
laboratory tests, developing enhanced surveillance techniques, and supporting 
Annual Certification. 
b. Develop and apply comprehensive methodologies, plans, and tools for 
certification, including high-energy density physics experiments, simulations, 
hydrodynamic testing, engineering sciences, and materials science. 
c. Develop options for the future nuclear deterrent working with the Department 
of War.

d. Maintain and enhance the existing nuclear weapons stockpile in accordance with 
Presidential Directives, the President’s annual Nuclear Weapons Stockpile 
Memorandum, and Nuclear Weapons Council planning. 
e. Incorporate enhanced surety features in alignment with Presidential direction and 
Nuclear Weapons Council planning. 
f. Develop and restore required manufacturing capabilities for identified 
weapon priorities. 
g. Plan, complete, and operate required NSE capital projects required to meet U.S. 
nuclear weapons mission activities. 
h. Be ready to conduct nuclear tests. 
i. Maintain a flexible, responsive, robust infrastructure, including research and 
development, engineering, production, and testing required to support U.S. 
nuclear weapons mission activities. 
j. Store and dismantle safely and securely nuclear weapons that have been removed 
from the stockpile. 
8. Conduct all NSE work consistent with the principles of protecting the environment and 
safeguarding the safety and health of the public and of the workforce.
